architectural_turning_points.blocking_evidence: No model-admissible continuous Rice-MAD land-adjustment domain, hard land cap, adjustment bound, or district water constraint was identified.
architectural_turning_points.original_element: Continuous district-level crop-area adjustment and optimization
architectural_turning_points.required_rewording: Replace continuous reallocation with a finite comparison of prespecified historically observed configurations.

architectural_turning_points.blocking_evidence: Only two complete, outcome-independent, empirically realized Rice-MAD configurations on 13 common districts passed the evidence rules.
architectural_turning_points.original_element: Optimization over a continuous crop-allocation set
architectural_turning_points.required_rewording: Describe C0B5-A2020-2021 and C0B5-A2023-2024 as fixed historical comparators, not feasible future solutions or recommendations.

architectural_turning_points.blocking_evidence: Common perennial initialization failed and nonlinear tail-risk cancellation of a shared perennial component is not valid.
architectural_turning_points.original_element: One five-crop A1/A2 portfolio and common Mean-CVaR comparison
architectural_turning_points.required_rewording: Keep five-crop characterization in Layer 1 and restrict the finite A1/A2 stress test to the Rice-MAD transient block in Layer 2.

architectural_turning_points.blocking_evidence: Crop outcome contracts have different temporal structures and the maximum current econometric interpretation is empirical association only.
architectural_turning_points.original_element: One homogeneous five-crop climate-yield and allocation model
architectural_turning_points.required_rewording: Use crop-specific temporal models and keep characterization separate from the finite reference stress test.

architectural_turning_points.blocking_evidence: The frozen D0 master provides seven Aug-Jul campaigns for Rice and MAD, with 646 usable outcomes and 61 preserved invalid rows.
architectural_turning_points.required_rewording: State the Rice-MAD outcome as district by crop by Aug-Jul campaign and retain crop-specific calendar-year contracts for perennials.

contribution_architecture.distinctive_component: A frozen, provenance-audited district-crop evidence chain linking agricultural outcomes, climate support, phenology, decision feasibility, and transient campaign outcomes.
contribution_architecture.established_method_not_novel: Version control, checksums, deterministic builds, and data-provenance reporting are established reproducibility practices.
contribution_architecture.novelty_limit: Do not claim a new reproducibility method or the first agricultural data pipeline.

contribution_architecture.distinctive_component: Crop-specific frozen windows and temporal attribution align climate measurement with Rice, MAD, Mango, Lemon, and Banana phenology in Piura.
contribution_architecture.established_method_not_novel: Phenology-aligned exposure construction is established scientific practice.
contribution_architecture.novelty_limit: Do not claim invention of phenological exposure methods.

contribution_architecture.distinctive_component: A prespecified dual temporal architecture permits heterogeneous crop-specific climate-yield associations without forcing all five crops into one model.
contribution_architecture.established_method_not_novel: Associational panel and time-series response models are established methods.
contribution_architecture.novelty_limit: Do not claim causal effects or globally invariant response functions.

contribution_architecture.distinctive_component: If future gates pass, one auditable chain will separate historical estimation, prospective ENSO scenario construction, prediction, economic translation, and risk measurement.
contribution_architecture.established_method_not_novel: Scenario simulation and downstream risk propagation are established methods.
contribution_architecture.novelty_limit: Do not claim that scenarios or risk estimates currently exist or that scenario tuning validates the historical model.

contribution_architecture.distinctive_component: Two prespecified historically observed Rice-MAD configurations can receive the same prospective scenario bank on 13 common districts.
contribution_architecture.established_method_not_novel: Stress testing fixed alternatives is established decision-analysis practice.
contribution_architecture.novelty_limit: Do not call either reference optimal, recommended, continuously feasible, or representative of a five-crop portfolio.

current_authorized_identity.general_objective: To characterize crop-specific associations between phenology-aligned climate exposures and district-level yields in Piura and, after separately frozen empirical-model and scenario designs, propagate those relationships through prospective ENSO 2026–2027 climate scenarios to characterize yield risk and compare two historically observed Rice–MAD reference configurations under a common scenario bank, with gross-production-value analysis retained only as a conditional extension subject to price-mapping and monetary-treatment gates.
current_authorized_identity.primary_research_question: How are phenology-aligned climate exposures associated with district-level yields across five focal crops in Piura, and what prospective ENSO 2026–2027 yield risks do these associations imply for crop-specific outcomes and for two historically observed Rice–MAD reference configurations evaluated under a common scenario bank?
current_authorized_identity.problem_statement: District-level agricultural climate-risk assessment in Piura requires a prespecified and reproducible design that respects crop-specific phenology and temporal outcome contracts while linking historical climate–yield associations to prospective ENSO 2026–2027 yield risk, a conditional secondary economic extension, and a common-scenario stress test of two historically observed Rice–MAD configurations. The current evidence identifies neither a continuous land-reallocation domain nor a five-crop portfolio, water-allocation model, or optimal future crop allocation.

specific_objectives.text: Characterize the crop-specific associations between prespecified phenology-aligned precipitation and temperature exposures and district-level yield outcomes within each frozen temporal contract.

Assess heterogeneity in crop-specific empirical climate–yield patterns and uncertainty using prespecified comparison rules that respect differences in estimand, scale, sample support, climate channel, phenological window, and temporal architecture.

Characterize prospective ENSO 2026–2027 yield-risk distributions and, only if the price-mapping and monetary-treatment gates pass, extend the authorized physical outcomes to corresponding gross-production-value risk.

Compare the prospective yield and conditionally authorized economic-risk profiles of C0B5-A2020-2021 and C0B5-A2023-2024 for Rice and MAD on their 13 common districts under an identical scenario bank and prespecified risk criteria.

subquestions.text: What crop-specific associations link prespecified phenology-aligned precipitation and temperature exposures to district-level yield outcomes within each frozen temporal contract?

How do crop-specific empirical climate–yield patterns and their uncertainty vary under prespecified comparison rules that respect differences in estimand, scale, sample support, climate channel, phenological window, and temporal architecture?

What prospective ENSO 2026–2027 yield-risk distributions arise from the separately specified scenario bank, and, if the price-mapping and monetary-treatment gates pass, what corresponding gross-production-value risk can be constructed?
How do the two historically observed Rice-MAD reference configurations compare on 13 common districts when evaluated with the same prospective scenario bank and prespecified risk criteria?

current_authorized_identity.working_title_v2: Phenology-Aligned Climate–Yield Associations and Prospective ENSO Risk in Piura, Peru: Five-Crop Evidence and Rice–Maize Reference Stress Tests

enso_role.A_historical_estimation: Estimate climate-yield associations using prespecified phenology-aligned climate exposures; ICEN is not automatically a direct district-yield regressor.
enso_role.B_state_and_context: Use ENSO indices and official state classifications to define and interpret large-scale climate context under a separately frozen design.
enso_role.C_prospective_2026_2027_scenarios: Construct prospective climate scenarios only after scenario-generator authorization; this is a prospective scenario stress context, the future realization is unknown, and no scenario currently exists.
enso_role.D_downstream_risk_propagation: After estimation and diagnostics, propagate the same authorized scenario bank through crop response, gated economic translation, and separately prespecified risk metrics.

failure_modes.preventive_design_rule: Freeze parsimonious Rice-MAD specifications, report effective degrees of freedom and small-sample uncertainty, and make no long-panel claim.
Use crop-specific low-dimensional specifications, disclose weak temporal depth, and avoid asymptotic overconfidence.
Freeze a strict complexity budget before estimation and prohibit specification search based on fit or coefficient significance.
Use the next outcome-blind adjudication gate based on phenology, completeness, support, interpretability, and measurement quality.
Quantify historical support, flag out-of-support scenario cells, and label projections as stress tests rather than forecasts when appropriate.
Freeze the scientific bridge from ENSO state to local precipitation and temperature scenarios before scenario generation.
Freeze price timing, nominal treatment, and aggregation rules; call the result gross production value, never profit.
Describe A1 and A2 as two fixed historical comparators and prohibit optimality, broad representativeness, interpolation, or recommendation claims.
Enforce the claim matrix and attribute novelty only to the integrated, reproducible application architecture.
Report Layer 1 and Layer 2 with separate estimands, samples, tables, and scope statements; never aggregate Layer 1 into A1/A2.

historical_working_identity.general_objective_reconstructed: Integrate district-level climate-yield estimation, El Niño 2026-2027 scenarios, economic valuation, and spatial Mean-CVaR to identify a crop allocation that maximizes expected agricultural value subject to downside risk.
historical_working_identity.intended_crop_allocation_interpretation_: A normative continuous district-level allocation across the target crops, interpreted as an optimized future allocation.
historical_working_identity.intended_decision_architecture_reconstru: A single five-crop spatial portfolio with continuous crop-area decision variables.
historical_working_identity.intended_enso_role_reconstructed: El Niño 2026-2027 provides the prospective climate-risk scenario context propagated into yield, economic value, and allocation decisions.
historical_working_identity.intended_mean_cvar_role_reconstructed: Mean-CVaR is the central optimization criterion balancing expected agricultural economic value and lower-tail risk.
historical_working_identity.problem_statement_reconstructed: Agricultural planning in Piura requires an allocation that protects economic value from district-level climate-yield losses under El Niño 2026-2027 risk.
historical_working_identity.research_question_reconstructed: How can district-level climate-yield relationships and El Niño 2026-2027 risk be integrated in a spatial Mean-CVaR model to optimize agricultural economic value and crop allocation in Piura?
specific_objectives_reconstructed: Estimate district-level climate-yield relationships for the target crops.
Generate prospective El Niño 2026-2027 climate and yield scenarios.
Translate crop outcomes into agricultural economic value.
Measure expected value and downside risk using Mean-CVaR.
Optimize spatial crop allocation across Piura districts.
